routeRationale: Issue carries labels `bug` + `route:bug-fleet`. A defect in a shipped command's contract, not a new capability, so it routes straight to the harness-debugging pipeline rather than through brainstorming -> autopilot. A bug lane leaves no plans/ directory by design.
scopeNote: CLI-R004 only; CLI-R006 (--json) is a symptom of #2069 and deliberately out of scope

stageDetail.sessionFileNote: .harness/debug/ is gitignored (.harness/.gitignore:4), so the session record is lane-local by repo policy; its findings are reproduced in this provenance file and in the PR body.

findings: packages/cli/src/commands/advise-skills.ts:85 — unconditional fs.writeFileSync(skillsMdPath, md) with no guard; skillsMdPath is a sibling of the user's spec.
Declared contract (lines 133-138) names no write: description 'Content-based skill recommendations for a spec', flags --spec-path/--thorough/--top/--json.
No existsSync check before the write, so a hand-edited SKILLS.md is clobbered silently; 'Written to <path>' is printed only after the fact.
git log -S 'fs.writeFileSync(skillsMdPath' returns a single commit 66ff7cf46 — present since the feature landed. An original design defect, not a regression.

Six in-repo commands already solve this exact problem identically: migrate.ts:562, migrate-backends.ts:181, rollback.ts:228, cleanup-sessions.ts:296, generate-slash-commands.ts:363, and the closest analogue align-design-system.ts:39 ('Compute diffs without writing files. Default: write.').
Shared shape: a dryRun?: boolean on the options interface defaulting to false, `if (!dryRun) { write }` at the write site, and output that states the plan. advise-skills simply never grew the guard.

phases.hypothesis: SKILLS.md appears next to the spec on every invocation because the write at line 85 is unconditional and no option can suppress it.
phases.test: Ran the real built CLI (packages/cli/dist/bin/harness.js) against a throwaway temp project seeded with a SKILLS.md containing 'I AM A HAND-EDITED FILE. DO NOT CLOBBER ME.'
phases.result: CONFIRMED — the hand-edited content was replaced by the generated markdown, and --dry-run was rejected by commander as an unknown option (exit 1).

phases.rootCause: The write was undeclared, unguarded, and impossible to preview — not that the command writes at all. Generating SKILLS.md is the advisor's advertised job.
changes: packages/cli/src/commands/advise-skills.ts — added dryRun?: boolean to AdviseSkillsOptions (default false, so the write stays opt-OUT); introduced an exported AdviseSkillsResult carrying written/existed; guarded the write; added --dry-run; description now names the write; formatWriteLine() distinguishes 'Written to' / 'Overwrote existing' / '[dry-run] Nothing written. Would create|overwrite <path>'.
docs/reference/cli-commands.md — regenerated via `pnpm run generate-docs` for the new flag and description.

mcpTwinUnchanged.proof: Invoked handleAdviseSkills() against a temp project after the fix: it still wrote SKILLS.md and still returned skillsPath='docs/changes/feat/SKILLS.md'; response key set unchanged (featureName,skillsPath,totalScanned,scanDuration,apply,reference,consider).
mcpTwinUnchanged.why: harness-planning/SKILL.md:62 instructs agents to run advise_skills to GENERATE SKILLS.md, and the MCP tool returns the resulting path. Inverting the default to opt-in would break both consumers, so the issue's ask — 'a guard and a dry-run' — was built rather than an inversion.

assumptions: The intended contract is 'advisor that generates SKILLS.md', not 'read-only query'. Grounded in two live consumers, not inferred: agents/skills/claude-code/harness-planning/SKILL.md:62 ('If SKILLS.md is missing but a spec exists: run the advisor inline using `advise_skills` MCP tool to generate SKILLS.md') and packages/cli/src/mcp/tools/advise-skills.ts:50 (returns skillsPath). Therefore the write stays ON by default and the fix is a guard plus a preview, never an inversion.

Named the option `dryRun` / `--dry-run` rather than the brief's suggested `write?: boolean`. Same semantics and the same default (write), but it matches the six existing in-repo precedents listed under the analyze phase, so the option reads the same way across the CLI. Deliberate, and disclosed in the PR body.

Correcting the MCP capability declaration for advise_skills from ['read'] to ['read','write'] is IN scope for CLI-R004: that register is the machine-readable form of the same defect. The file's own header calls itself 'AUTHORITATIVE, evidence-based', says entries are 'derived by reading the tool's handler', and defines `read` as 'none of the above; observation only' — while the handler calls writeFileSync. `harness mcp list-capabilities`, the adopter audit surface, was therefore reporting a writing tool as observation-only.

That correction carries zero behavioral risk: the declaration is consumed for REPORTING only (tool-capabilities.ts, commands/mcp.ts); server.ts:438-445 merges it onto the tool definition and nothing authorizes or gates against it. The coverage test tests/commands/mcp-list-capabilities.test.ts pins scopes for run_ci_checks/run_skill/outcome_eval only, not advise_skills, and passes unchanged.

The new tests live in a NEW file (advise-skills-write-guard.test.ts) rather than the existing advise-skills.test.ts because that suite mocks node:fs wholesale and so can only observe that writeFileSync was called. This defect is about a file appearing on disk, so the new suite keeps node:fs REAL and asserts against an actual temp dir, mocking only the expensive collaborators. Two test files per command is an established pattern here (check-operational-drift.test.ts / check-operational-drift-action.test.ts). Both suites pass; the pre-existing one was not modified, which is itself evidence the default behavior is unchanged.

Mocking loadOrRebuildIndex in the new suite is load-bearing, not incidental: index-builder.ts:189-190 writes a .harness/skills-index.json cache into projectRoot, and the real builder scans machine-global skill directories (785 skills on this host), which would make the suite slow and machine-dependent.

CLI-R006 (--json) was deliberately NOT fixed. Confirmed as #2069's shadowing defect: the root program declares --json first and Commander is first-declarer-wins. The local .option('--json', ...) declaration was left byte-for-byte untouched. Reported, not repaired.
CLI-R001 (flag naming, polish/small) was out of scope and untouched.
All build/test/docs steps ran under Node 22 (v22.23.2) per the repo's .husky/ensure-node-pin.sh; the ambient shell is Node 24, under which better-sqlite3 is ABI-mismatched.
